title: feat(cl,app): unwind continuous C at clear links against the machine's stated C travel
body:
Slice 2 of #33 (continuous C-axis live tooling). This covers item 2 of the 2026-11-08 owed list: unwinding C on links against a stated travel.

## What changed
- **`cl::unwind_c`** (new `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary_unwind.rs`) takes a path stamped by `stamp_c` and brings every stated C inside the machine's C travel by whole turns.
  - The path is split at its clear links. A clear link is a point the tool reached by a rapid that stands at the path's own clearance (the highest rapid Z, or the largest rapid radius), and only where that clearance is strictly beyond every cut point (feed and plunge ends, feed starts). On a standing bar's Rotary Contour, that is the point between each ring's retract and the next ring's plunge.
  - A stretch that fits the travel is left as stamped. A stretch that does not fit is moved by the fewest whole turns.
  - Each rewind is written into the path as the part-frame orbit it really is: rapid chords round the circle through the link point, each stating its C and the radial station pose, split so the machine's C-linear arc stays within the op tolerance. Verify, the solid bar audit, the steel laws and the post therefore all see it.
  - Refused by name:
    - a stretch whose own C span cannot fit the travel ("... no clear link stands inside it to unwind at");
    - a travel that is not a range;
    - a non-finite point;
    - a path whose moves do not chain;
    - a rewind needing more than 100 000 chords;
    - a path with index-keyed records where an orbit must be inserted.
- **`rotary_gate::stamp_spindle_c`** reads the travel from the machine's rotary named C, the same axis `machine::check`'s C letter gate judges.
  - **Rotary Contour** unwinds.
  - **Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset do not unwind** (review round 1, decision below).
- **The C feed cap (review round 1).** `fanuc-lathe.cps` caps every C block's composite F so that neither part of the move outruns the machine file. The X/Z part stays within `machine.feedRateMax`, and the C part stays within the C rate the machine states (its normal speed, else its rapid speed).
  - The script's rotary inventory now carries each rotary's own `speeds` (deg/min). They still stay out of every mm/min field.
  - Where the machine file states no C rate, C is not capped: the rotary rate is unbounded by data on such a machine.
  - Rewinds stay coordinated G01 moves, because a G00 with C is not coordinated and would leave the verified chord.

## Review round 1 - what was fixed
1. **Scope: Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset took the refusal path, not end-to-end tests.** On a machine that states a C travel, each posts only a path whose stamped C already fits the travel, which is what the machine check passed before this PR. Where C would need a rewind, generation refuses by name: "... unwinding C at links is proven for Rotary Contour only, so {kind} is refused where it would need a rewind".
   - Pinned by `operation::rotary_gate::tests::parallel_and_offset_are_refused_by_name_where_c_would_need_a_rewind`. The same test pins the contrast: the contour unwinds the same helix.
   - Why not end-to-end tests: Rotary Parallel on the spindle's C needs a bar leaning 1-2.6 deg off Z. It refuses a standing bar, and the C gate refuses anything leaning further, so no honest fixture exists. Rotary Offset's end-to-end fixture is the slow center_cut_multiaxis kind. Neither fit the time box.
   - Recorded in `docs/decisions/33-c-unwind.md`.
2. **The posted rewind feed.** The cap rule: F = min(composite, `feedRateMax * lcmd / lin`, `C rate * lcmd / |dC|`), with C uncapped when no C rate is stated.
   - The unwind golden now posts the orbit at **F6000** (the bench states C 6000 deg/min, like the shipped `millturn.mch`; was F22954). The retract posts at **F4000**, the stated linear feed.
   - `assert_feeds_within` reads every posted C block back and checks its X/Z and C rates against the machine's stated limits. It runs on the golden and on the Rotary Contour program.
   - `a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed`: a machine stating 1000 mm/min and C 500 deg/min posts a lower maximum F, every block within its limits.
   - **No existing golden moves.** `c_axis_helix.nc` (slice 1) is byte-identical: its machine states no C rate, and the linear cap never binds below the composite value. `c_axis_live`'s golden test passes unchanged.
3. **Hardening.** `unwind_c` now refuses a non-finite point (`a_non_finite_point_refuses_by_name`) and a broken chain (`a_broken_chain_refuses_by_name`) by name.

## Review round 2 - what was fixed
1. **The radial-clearance link is now opt-in, and off for every shipped kind.** `unwind_c` takes a `radial` flag. The retract cylinder (a rapid at a radius strictly beyond every cut) counts as a clear link only when the caller admits it. Rotary Contour, the only kind that unwinds, does not.
   - **Why not a radial end-to-end case:** no op parameter decides the contour's link kind. The waterline kernel always links rings over the axial clearance plane (`clearance_z`, or `retract_z` when set), and its rapids stand at the rings' own radii. No honest radial-link contour fixture exists, and no shipped op can reach the radial branch now.
   - **Refusal:** a contour stretch whose only clear point is radial is refused by name: "... no clear link stands inside it to unwind at (a retract cylinder stands beyond the cut, but radial links are not taken for this kind)".
   - **Pins for the branch itself (`cl::rotary_unwind::tests`):**
     - `a_radial_link_beyond_the_cut_unwinds_at_its_radius_when_admitted`: three rings joined by radial links at r 20, with no axial clearance. Every added move is a rewind chord with both ends at r 20, the chain holds, and every C is inside -360..360.
     - `a_radial_link_at_or_inside_the_cut_radius_is_no_link`: a link at r 10 (equal to the cut radius) or at r 5 (inside it) is no link, and the unwind is refused by name.
     - `a_radial_only_link_is_refused_by_name_where_radial_links_are_not_admitted`: the same path with `radial = false` is refused, with the reason in the message.
   - **Pin for the wiring:** `operation::rotary_gate::tests::the_contour_takes_no_radial_link` sends the radial-link path through Rotary Contour's own gate and gets the named refusal.
2. **The Parallel/Offset gap from round 1 is closed by refusal: they never unwind.** On a stated C travel they post only what fits as stamped, and are refused by name where C would need a rewind (`parallel_and_offset_are_refused_by_name_where_c_would_need_a_rewind`). No rewind move can be emitted for them.
## Pinning tests
- `c_axis_unwind`:
  - `a_rotary_contour_on_a_stated_c_travel_unwinds_at_its_links_and_posts`
  - `a_rewind_through_stock_is_convicted_by_the_verifier`
  - `a_ring_wider_than_the_stated_travel_refuses_by_name`
  - `two_rings_unwound_post_to_their_golden`
  - `a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed`
- `cl::rotary_unwind::tests` (8): the three radial-link tests above, plus:
  - `three_rings_unwind_at_their_links_and_stay_a_chain`
  - `a_path_inside_its_travel_comes_back_unchanged`
  - `a_ring_wider_than_the_travel_refuses_by_name`
  - `a_non_finite_point_refuses_by_name`
  - `a_broken_chain_refuses_by_name`
- `operation::rotary_gate::tests::parallel_and_offset_are_refused_by_name_where_c_would_need_a_rewind`, `operation::rotary_gate::tests::the_contour_takes_no_radial_link`

## Goldens
- **Added in this PR:** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_unwind.nc`. This round it moved in its own commit (`5c582cd5`), from F22954 to F6000 on the orbit, caused by the feed cap.
- **Existing goldens moved:** none.

## Gate
This round changed non-test code (the radial opt-in), so the full gate ran on the final head ff0fb3924e990280994989b9cd1bb486e455d820, with origin/main 4c3f7565 merged in. It used `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, which falls back to batch scope for a `cl` change. 9/9 steps green in 43.1 min: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app (including `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind` and `rotary_letter`), ui from crates/ui, and clippy -D warnings on all eight crates. Nothing was pushed after it. The earlier rounds' gates were green on 3a6ff68e and 5c582cd5.

## Not exercised
- Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset end to end on a C. Their refusal is pinned at the gate they both pass through.
- `check_document` on an unwound op. The travel bounds are asserted directly.
- A real control: owed item 5, the composite feed law.

## Still owed on #33
1. A machine C-sense word.
3. Axial/face live-tool stations and G12.1 polar interpolation.
4. Arcs on a C turn.
5. Confirming the composite (degree-as-mm) rotary feed law on a real control.
6. live_tool words in a shipped machine.
- Unwinding for Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset (closed for this PR by refusal: they never unwind). Admitting the radial link for them needs an end-to-end fixture each.
- Owed on a real control (with item 5): the composite reading of F (X radius, Z and C-as-mm), the rewind as G01 at a composite feed in place of a G00, and the machine check on an unwound op at document level.
- Follow-up worth filing: fanuc.cps and doosan-dnm.cps write C on combined moves with no C-rate cap. This predates this PR.
- Possibly: a control roll-over word as an alternative to orbit rewinds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/33-c-unwind.md`.
No new user-facing command, so no MCP tool is owed.
Effort: high (not escalated).

Changelog: Continuous C-axis live tooling unwinds C at clear links against the machine's stated C travel (Rotary Contour; Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset refuse by name where C would need a rewind). Each rewind is an orbit the verifier and the post see, and the lathe post caps every C block's feed by the machine's stated linear feed and C rate (#33)

Refs #33
